question: Human development also involves freedom, security and dignity in life. The first Human Development Report was published in which year? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1971
1990
1995
1980
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1990

Explanation:
The first Human Development Report was published in 1990 by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). This report introduced a new way of measuring development by focusing on people's capabilities, not just economic growth. It defined human development as expanding people's freedoms and opportunities, including freedom, security, and dignity. The report also introduced the Human Development Index (HDI), which combines indicators of health, education, and income. The Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq is credited as the chief architect of the report. Since then, the HDR has been published annually, providing a comprehensive assessment of global human development.

☛ Which organization publishes HDR? → UNDP
☛ Key index introduced in HDR? → Human Development Index (HDI)
☛ Three dimensions of HDI? → Health, Education, Income
☛ Chief architect of first HDR? → Mahbub ul Haq
question_hi: मानव विकास में जीवन में स्वतंत्रता, सुरक्षा और गरिमा भी शामिल है। पहली मानव विकास रिपोर्ट किस वर्ष प्रकाशित हुई थी? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which institution played a major role in supporting India’s liberalisation policy during the 1991 crisis? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Reserve Bank of India
Election Commission of India
NITI Aayog
International Monetary Fund (IMF)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is International Monetary Fund (IMF)

Explanation:
In 1991, India faced a severe balance of payments crisis, with foreign exchange reserves sufficient for only two weeks of imports. To overcome this situation, the Indian government sought a loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The IMF imposed conditions that required India to undertake comprehensive economic reforms, including liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation (LPG). The IMF's guidance and financial support pushed India towards economic reforms, opening its economy to global markets. Thus, during the 1991 crisis, the IMF played a major role in supporting India's liberalisation policy.

☛ What is the full form of LPG policy? → Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation
☛ Where is the IMF headquarters located? → Washington D.C., United States
☛ Which currency did India devalue after taking the IMF loan in 1991? → Rupee
☛ In which year did India start economic reforms? → 1991
question_hi: 1991 के संकट के दौरान भारत की उदारीकरण नीति का समर्थन करने में किस संस्था ने प्रमुख भूमिका निभाई? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)

नीति आयोग

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF)

Explanation:
1991 में भारत को गंभीर भुगतान संतुलन संकट का सामना करना पड़ा, जिसमें विदेशी मुद्रा भंडार केवल दो सप्ताह के आयात के लिए पर्याप्त रह गया था। इस स्थिति से उबरने के लिए भारत सरकार ने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF) से ऋण लिया। IMF ने ऋण देने के लिए शर्त रखी कि भारत को व्यापक आर्थिक सुधार करने होंगे, जिनमें उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण (LPG) शामिल थे। IMF के मार्गदर्शन और वित्तीय सहायता ने भारत को आर्थिक सुधारों की दिशा में प्रेरित किया, जिससे भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था खुली और वैश्विक बाजारों से जुड़ गई। इस प्रकार, 1991 के संकट के दौरान IMF ने भारत की उदारीकरण नीति का समर्थन करने में प्रमुख भूमिका निभाई।

question: What is the key reason governments promote Public-Private Partnerships in infrastructure development?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: To address fiscal constraints and reduce liabilities
To improve efficiency and innovation through private sector expertise
Due to lack of trained manpower
To privatise all national resources
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To improve efficiency and innovation through private sector expertise

Explanation:
Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) involve collaboration between government and private sector for infrastructure projects. The primary reason is to leverage the private sector's efficiency, technical knowledge, and innovation, which reduces costs and improves quality. While addressing fiscal constraints is a benefit, it is not the key reason. PPP is not aimed at privatizing resources or addressing lack of trained manpower. Private participation ensures risk sharing and timely project completion. The private sector brings advanced technology and management practices, leading to better project outcomes. Governments provide regulatory support and land acquisition, making PPP a balanced model.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Full form of PPP → Public-Private Partnership
☛ Main benefit of PPP → Improved efficiency and innovation
☛ PPP usage in India → Roads, ports, energy projects
☛ Government role in PPP → Regulatory framework and land acquisition
☛ Private sector role in PPP → Design, finance, construction, and operation

Explanation:
सार्वजनिक-निजी भागीदारी (PPP) में सरकार और निजी क्षेत्र मिलकर बुनियादी ढांचा परियोजनाओं को क्रियान्वित करते हैं। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य निजी क्षेत्र की दक्षता, तकनीकी ज्ञान और नवाचार का लाभ उठाना है, जिससे परियोजनाओं की लागत कम होती है और गुणवत्ता बेहतर होती है। वित्तीय बाधाओं को दूर करना भी एक लाभ है, लेकिन यह मुख्य कारण नहीं है। PPP का उद्देश्य संसाधनों का निजीकरण या प्रशिक्षित जनशक्ति की कमी को दूर करना नहीं है। निजी क्षेत्र की भागीदारी से जोखिम साझा होता है और परियोजनाओं का समय पर पूरा होना सुनिश्चित होता है।

question: What was one of the major characteristics of India’s economy at the time of independence in 1947? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Self-sufficiency in manufacturing
Strong trade surplus
Heavy dependence on agriculture and low productivity
Dominance of the services sector
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Heavy dependence on agriculture and low productivity

Explanation:
At independence in 1947, India's economy was characterized by heavy dependence on agriculture and low productivity. About 85% of the population depended on agriculture, but productivity was very low due to lack of technology and irrigation. Industry and services sectors were underdeveloped. There was no strong trade surplus, and India was not self-sufficient in manufacturing. The British colonial policies had turned India into an exporter of raw materials and importer of finished goods.

☛ Share of agriculture in India's GDP at independence → over 50%
☛ Main objective of British economic policy in India → serving British interests
☛ Type of economic planning adopted by India after independence → mixed economy and Five-Year Plans
☛ Revolution started to boost agricultural productivity in India → Green Revolution

Solution: सही उत्तर है कृषि पर भारी निर्भरता और कम उत्पादकता

Explanation:
1947 में स्वतंत्रता के समय भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था की मुख्य विशेषता कृषि पर भारी निर्भरता और निम्न उत्पादकता थी। लगभग 85% जनसंख्या कृषि पर निर्भर थी, लेकिन प्रौद्योगिकी और सिंचाई की कमी के कारण उत्पादकता बहुत कम थी। उद्योग और सेवा क्षेत्र अविकसित थे। व्यापार अधिशेष नहीं था और विनिर्माण में आत्मनिर्भरता नहीं थी। ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान विदेशी व्यापार नीति ने भारत को कच्चे माल का निर्यातक और तैयार माल का आयातक बना दिया था।

question: What has been the trend in India’s per capita income since the 1991 reforms?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: No significant change
Constant decline
Fluctuating without a pattern
Gradual increase
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gradual increase

Explanation:
Since the 1991 economic reforms, India's per capita income has shown a gradual increase. The reforms adopted liberalization, privatization, and globalization policies, which accelerated economic growth. In 1990-91, per capita income was around $1,200, which rose to about $2,500 by 2023-24. Although the growth has been slow, it has been positive and steady. India maintained relatively good growth even during global recessions. The increase in per capita income is mainly due to the expansion of the services sector, foreign investment, and technological advancement.

☛ How is per capita income calculated in India? → By dividing national income by total population

☛ Which sector grew the fastest after the 1991 reforms? → Services sector
☛ What is the impact of rising per capita income on standard of living? → It improves the standard of living

Solution: सही उत्तर है धीरे-धीरे वृद्धि

Explanation:
1991 के आर्थिक सुधारों के बाद भारत की प्रति व्यक्ति आय में निरंतर वृद्धि देखी गई है। इन सुधारों के तहत उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण की नीतियां अपनाई गईं, जिससे आर्थिक वृद्धि दर में तेजी आई। 1990-91 में प्रति व्यक्ति आय लगभग 1,200 डॉलर थी, जो 2023-24 तक बढ़कर लगभग 2,500 डॉलर हो गई। हालांकि वृद्धि धीमी रही है, लेकिन यह सकारात्मक और स्थिर रही है। वैश्विक मंदी के दौरान भी भारत ने अपेक्षाकृत अच्छी वृद्धि बनाए रखी। प्रति व्यक्ति आय में वृद्धि का मुख्य कारण सेवा क्षेत्र का विस्तार, विदेशी निवेश और तकनीकी प्रगति है।

question: Which sector in India saw significant growth due to globalisation and outsourcing after the 1990s? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Agriculture
Mining
Real Estate
IT and Services
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is IT and Services

Explanation:
After the 1990s, globalisation and outsourcing led to significant growth in India's IT and services sector. Following economic reforms in 1991, foreign companies began outsourcing their services to India to reduce costs, giving the Indian IT industry global recognition. Cities like Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Pune became hubs of this growth. This sector not only created employment opportunities but also contributed significantly to India's service exports, making India a major player in the global IT outsourcing market.

question: Liberalisation reduced government control over economic activities. What did liberalisation in 1991 primarily aim to eliminate? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Banking services
Industrial licensing and quota system
Public sector employment
Agricultural subsidies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Industrial licensing and quota system

Explanation:
The primary aim of liberalisation in 1991 was to eliminate the industrial licensing and quota system, commonly known as the 'License Raj'. Under this system, private companies required government permission for production, expansion, and investment, which hindered business growth and slowed economic development. As part of liberalisation, most industries were exempted from licensing requirements, except for a few related to environment and security. This move reduced government control over economic activities, promoted private sector participation, and integrated India into the global economy. The reforms marked a shift from a protectionist economy to a market-oriented one, boosting industrial growth and efficiency.

question: Which of the following sectors includes banking, communication and transport? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Quaternary
Secondary

solution:

Explanation:

The tertiary sector includes all services that support production and distribution. Banking provides financial services, communication enables information exchange, and transport ensures movement of goods and people. These services are essential for the smooth functioning of the economy. The quaternary sector involves knowledge-based services like research and IT, while the tertiary sector provides services directly to consumers.

question: Which of the following best defines globalisation in the context of economic reforms in India, post 1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (20/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Closure of multinational companies
Integration of the Indian economy with the global economy

Promoting only domestic trade
solution:

Explanation:
Globalisation in the context of post-1991 economic reforms in India refers to the integration of the Indian economy with the global economy. The New Economic Policy (1991) emphasised liberalisation, privatisation, and globalisation. Barriers to trade, investment, and technology were reduced. Foreign investment was encouraged, and import-export policies were liberalised. The goal was to connect India to global supply chains and accelerate economic growth. Multinational companies were allowed to enter Indian markets, increasing competition and efficiency. As a result, India's foreign exchange reserves grew, and the economy became more open and globally integrated.

question: What percentage of the Indian population was dependent on agriculture around the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: About 30%
About 90%
About 50%
About 70%
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is About 70%

Explanation:
At the time of independence in 1947, India's economy was predominantly agrarian, with approximately 70% of the population dependent on agriculture for their livelihood. The agricultural sector contributed around 50% to the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP). This high dependence reflected the lack of industrialization under British rule and the predominance of a rural economy. Agriculture was mostly of subsistence nature, heavily reliant on monsoons, with low productivity due to outdated techniques. Landholdings were small and fragmented, resulting in poor economic conditions for farmers. Despite the large agricultural workforce, the country faced food shortages, which led to tragedies like the Bengal Famine of 1943. This dependency underscores the importance of later agricultural reforms and the Green Revolution.

question: Colonial policies significantly altered India’s trade structure. Which of the following best describes India’s foreign trade pattern at the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Export of capital goods and import of consumer goods
Export of finished goods and import of raw materials
Balanced trade between agriculture and industry
Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods

Explanation:
Under colonial policies, British rule turned India into a source of raw materials and a market for finished goods. India exported raw materials like cotton, jute, tea, and indigo, while importing manufactured goods such as textiles, machinery, and other industrial products from Britain. This one-sided trade structure hindered India's industrial development. At the time of independence, India's foreign trade pattern was predominantly based on exporting raw materials and importing manufactured goods, a direct outcome of colonial exploitation. This pattern persisted because the British deliberately de-industrialized India and promoted its own manufacturing sector.

question: How did the Industrial Revolution alter the British economic interests in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: From taxes to feudal rule
From plantations to nomadic life
From control to cultural ties
From trade to industry and raw material use
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is From trade to industry and raw material use

Explanation:
The Industrial Revolution transformed Britain into a factory-based economy, requiring vast quantities of raw materials. India became a source of raw cotton, indigo, jute, and tea for British industries, while British manufactured goods flooded Indian markets. This destroyed India's traditional handicraft industries and restructured the Indian economy as a supplier of raw materials and a consumer of British goods. British policies deliberately de-industrialized India, shifting economic interests from merely trading Indian goods to controlling raw material extraction and industrial markets. Thus, British interests shifted from trade to industry and raw material use.

question: Which of the following sectors employed the largest share of India’s population before independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

Agriculture
Services
Trade
solution:

Explanation:
Before independence, India's economy was predominantly based on agriculture. Nearly 70-75% of the population was employed in this sector. The British colonial policies led to stagnation and inefficiency in the agricultural sector, with most people engaged in subsistence farming or working as agricultural laborers. question: In which of the following years was the monetary policy framework moved towards flexible inflation targeting and a six member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) constituted for setting the policy rate? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 1992
2016
2013
1998
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2016

Explanation:
The monetary policy framework in India was moved towards flexible inflation targeting and a six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) for setting the policy rate was constituted in the year 2016. This change followed the Monetary Policy Framework Agreement signed between the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Government of India in 2015. Under this agreement, the RBI was mandated to keep inflation within the range of 4% (±2%). The new framework was implemented by amending the RBI Act, 1934 in 2016. The MPC consists of three members from the RBI and three external experts, who decide on the policy rate.

question: Which of the following options best defines 'Sustainable Development'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Industrialisation without any restrictions
Maximising profits from natural resources
Using only renewable resources
Development that meets present needs without compromising future generations
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Development that meets present needs without compromising future generations

Explanation:
The concept of Sustainable Development was introduced in the 1987 Brundtland Report. Its main goal is to balance economic growth, social equity, and environmental protection. It ensures that the needs of the present generation are met without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It is based on three pillars: economic, social, and environmental sustainability. Examples include promoting renewable energy, conserving forests, and controlling pollution. This definition differs from other options because it emphasizes a long-term perspective rather than short-term gains. Sustainable Development is also the foundation of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) adopted by the UN in 2015.
